doc.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023

title: Guitar section with Bucky Pizzarelli and a hard rehearsal band
summary: He played one date with Bucky Pizzarelli and recalls a rehearsal band whose music was too difficult, with Bert Collins reading it easily.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Did you ever sit in the guitar section with Bucky Pizzarelli?

Only on one date, yeah. And it was for a piano player by the name of Charles Coleman. I don’t know anything about his career anymore. Charles was one of the players at the Playboy Club when I was there and he was doing this date and he had me called in for that date and Bucky was the other guitar player on it.

Well going back to those clarinet etudes you were playing on guitar, your reading must have gotten pretty strong. I’m wondering if you ever found yourself in a situation with a piece of guitar music in front of you going oh my, this is like, I need to woodshed this before I can play it?

Yeah, well yeah absolutely. I participated in a rehearsal band with — I think it was Adolph Sandole or Dennis Sandole, one of the guys. And they had — the music was just so difficult, I’m telling you now, in my lifetime I might not be able to play it at the speed it was to be played at. It just was physically not in my capabilities. Maybe someone else could have done it but it would have taken years for me to have that under my fingers and maybe never ever get it. But there was a trumpet player on this — when you brought this up it immediately brought this scene back to mind. The music was difficult and this trumpet player ripped through it like he had been reading it all his life. It was Bert Collins. Bert was a studio musician and also did a lot of Broadway work, but brilliant trumpet player. And I’ll tell you, I was embarrassed to be that far away from where I should have been on that topic. So the studies that I did came in handy but every once in a while you’d be thrown a curve like that that you couldn’t hit, or that I couldn’t hit anyway.
